source.title: Sharpness-aware Federated Graph Learning
source.authors: Ruiyu Li; Peige Zhao; Guangxia Li; Peng-Cheng Wu; Xing-Yu Gao; Zhiqiang Xu

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper, though some figures and table layout are flattened in extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sharpness-aware training and representation decorrelation to federated graph classification, a new setting for generalization results, and reports test performance and a sharpness comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for federated GNN methods and compares the generalization gap only qualitatively through loss landscapes. Its result tables compare methods and RepDec conditions; they do not report training and test error together or a measured generalization gap. Sharpness values are not numerically measured. Results cited from earlier work are excluded.
record.test_reason: SEAL uses the presumed connection between flat minima and generalization to design a training method. Its results compare method performance and qualitative loss landscapes, without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness against training–test error gaps at similarly low training loss. These results do not test V7 or another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: SEAL combines sharpness-aware optimization and representation decorrelation to improve federated graph classification and claimed generalization across heterogeneous settings. This is a conclusion about their method's performance, not validation of V7's sharpness–gap correlation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adaptive sharpness-aware minimization and a representation decorrelation regularizer in federated graph learning; it does not reproduce the magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap analysis in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that performance depends on the selected regularizer coefficient α and perturbation radius ρ; α performance first improves then degrades, while test accuracy with increasing ρ initially improves and then saturates or slightly decreases. For local epochs, performance first improves, saturates, then drops slightly.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 qualitatively shows flatter local loss landscapes for SEAL than FedAvg in non-IID COLLAB, Chem, and BioChemSn. Tables 1–3 report improved held-out accuracy for the proposed training methods, but do not pair these landscapes with measured training–test error gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware optimization combined with representation decorrelation can improve held-out graph-classification accuracy in heterogeneous federated learning.

record.peer_reviewed: Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM ’26), as stated in the paper front matter.
record.problems: The loss-landscape comparison uses a randomly selected representative client and is qualitative; no numeric sharpness or training-test generalization gap is reported. Test-accuracy tables report means and standard deviations across five runs, but not train-test error pairs.
record.rows_left_out: No other V7 rows were extracted: Figure 4 has only the three reported settings (Non-IID COLLAB, Chem, BioChemSn). Tables 1–6 report method/test-accuracy or hyperparameter results, not the magnitude-aware sharpness-to-generalization-gap relation named by V7.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting and natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison. Adaptive sharpness refers to weight-scaled perturbations, not an Adam-like optimizer comparison.
No controlled batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention; representation decorrelation is a different regularizer.

No measured relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and training–test error gaps among similarly fitted networks, and no ranking comparison with norm- or margin-based measures. Weight-scaled perturbations are used for optimization rather than evaluated as a generalization measure.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of a quantified sharpness–gap analysis makes V7 untested, rather than absent or challenged. The scale-invariance discussion in Section 4.1 draws on prior work and motivates the optimizer; it supplies no independent test of V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; no random-label experiments.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.

The paper compares loss-landscape flatness qualitatively for FedAvg and SEAL, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or report its relation to the training-test gap. The flatness figure gives no recoverable numeric values.
